sections.title: Executive investment summary: a scale assembler at a policy hinge, priced for a different business

blocks.text: Dixon is an Indian electronics manufacturing services (EMS) and original design manufacturing (ODM) group. It assembles smartphones and feature phones, telecom customer-premises equipment, laptops, LED TVs, refrigerators and washing machines for brand owners, and it is now adding components such as camera modules and display modules [F] (AR2026 p.78-81). In plain terms it is paid a conversion charge on a bill of materials that the customer largely specifies. Management describes mobile revenue as 'a function of the bill of material ... plus our conversion charge', with an 'EBITDA per unit' agreed by complexity [MC] (CALL May 2026). Group EMS work was about 89% of revenue and ODM/components about 11% [MC] (AR2026 p.98).

**End markets.** FY26 revenue mix was Mobile and Other EMS 91%, Consumer Electronics and Refrigerators 6%, Home Appliances 3% [F] (AR2026 p.78). Lighting went into a 50:50 joint venture with Signify from 1 August 2025 and is no longer consolidated [F] (AR2026 p.505). **Geography.** Domestic revenue was Rs 43,452 cr and exports Rs 5,421 cr in FY26, against Rs 37,118 cr and Rs 1,742 cr in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.467). Exports therefore rose from about 4.5% to about 11.1% of revenue [E] (AR2026 p.467). **Customers.** Three customers made up about 62% of consolidated revenue in FY26, up from 60% in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.497). Named customers include Motorola, Samsung, HP, Asus, Acer, Lenovo, Airtel (through the telecom subsidiary), Transsion-group entities (through Ismartu) and Eureka Forbes [F] (AR2026 p.23-44, p.141, p.228; CALL Oct 2025; CALL May 2026).

**Listing status.** Dixon is not a recent listing. It was incorporated in 1993 and has ten years of consolidated statements in our dataset [F] (AR2026 p.236; NUMBERS). An investor on the October 2025 call referred to the company raising capital in 2017 [F] (CALL Oct 2025), but the annual report does not restate the IPO date [F] (AR2026 p.156). No prospectus was available to us, so the pre-2017 history rests on the company's own timeline [AI].

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. **Valuation detached from every modelled case.** Price Rs 12,774 vs DCF per-share values of Rs -665.8 (bear), Rs 2,271.4 (base) and Rs 6,233.2 (bull). The reverse DCF needs about 84% annual sales growth for five years, against 19.8% in the base case [F] (NUMBERS).

2. **Thin, falling operating margin.** Q1 FY27 operating margin was 3.0% vs 3.8% a year earlier [F] (PPT Aug 2026). The mobile segment margin was 2.6% [F] (PPT Aug 2026), below the 2.8-3.2% range management indicated in January [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Management expects no margin improvement in FY27 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

3. **Reported earnings flattered by investment gains.** Other income was 35.3% of FY26 PBT [F] (NUMBERS). Q1 FY27 PAT of Rs 718 cr includes a Rs 519 cr fair-value gain on Aditya Infotech; adjusted PAT after minority interest was Rs 218 cr, down 3% [F] (PPT Aug 2026).
4. **Severe customer concentration.** The top three customers are about 62% of revenue, rising [F] (AR2026 p.497). Names and amounts are not disclosed [F] (AR2026 p.497; CALL Oct 2025).

5. **PLI receivable risk.** The auditor flagged with an emphasis of matter Rs 1,110 cr of PLI 'overflow' incentive accrued but not yet determined by the government agency, against a Rs 726 cr pass-through liability to the customer [F] (AR2026 p.409, p.509).

6. **Guidance credibility.** FY26 smartphone volume guidance of 40-42m (Oct 2025) ended at about 32-33m. The FY27 telecom target was cut from Rs 7,500-8,000 cr to Rs 6,700-7,000 cr within one quarter. Vivo approval was 'coming weeks' in October 2025 and arrived in July 2026 [MC] (CALL Oct 2025; CALL May 2026; CALL Aug 2026).
7. **Working-capital reversal.** In Q1 FY27 inventories rose from Rs 3,837 cr to Rs 6,728 cr. CFO was Rs -341 cr and FCF Rs -676 cr [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

8. **Value leakage to JV partners.** NCI took Rs 205.6 cr of FY26 profit [F] (AR2026 p.419). The growth vehicles are 51-74% owned: Vivo 51%, Longcheer 74%, Inventec 60%, HKC 74%, Gemtek 60% [F] (AR2026 p.141-146; ANNOUNCEMENTS; CALL Oct 2025).

9. **Policy dependency.** Mobile PLI 1 expired in March 2026 and took about 0.5% of mobile margin with it [MC] (CALL Feb 2026; CALL Aug 2026). The FY27-FY28 margin path depends on PLI 2 and ECMS rules that, per management, are still awaited [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
10. **Promoter selling.** The promoter group fell from 33.80% (Sep 2023) to 28.55% (Jun 2026) [F] (NUMBERS). Sunil Vachani sold about 19.75 lakh shares in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.348-349).

**Is the margin trough temporary?** Bull: percentage margins are optically diluted by memory-price pass-through and absolute per-unit profit is intact [MC] (CALL May 2026). Bear: the absolute figures also fell. Adjusted EBITDA was Rs 472 cr vs Rs 484 cr and adjusted PAT Rs 218 cr vs Rs 225 cr [F] (PPT Aug 2026). The 'optical' explanation does not cover a decline in absolute profit [AI].

**Are components a moat or a capex sink?** The display JV needs Rs 1,100-1,200 cr of capex [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Q Tech carries Rs 523 cr of goodwill and had negative net assets of Rs -82.9 cr at FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.505, p.507). The market may be underestimating execution and integration risk [AI].

**Is concentration risk or stickiness?** Several large customers are also JV partners: Airtel via Beetel, Transsion via Ismartu, the Q Tech parent, and Longcheer [F] (AR2026 p.23-58). That raises switching costs but means the customer captures part of the value through NCI and pricing [AI].
**Does the market overvalue policy?** PLI 2 and ECMS are real tailwinds, but the documents contain no notified PLI 2 guidelines. All quantification is management's understanding [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**Could the market be too bearish on cash?** FY26 FCF was Rs 724 cr and 3-year CFO/PAT was 1.08x [F] (NUMBERS). If Q1 FY27 inventory build is truly strategic, it unwinds and cash conversion stays good [AI].

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus framing is that Dixon is a high-growth compounder in a temporary margin air pocket. Our reading of the evidence is different. Dixon is a 3-4% margin assembler. Its reported earnings growth in FY26 and Q1 FY27 came mainly from mark-to-market gains on a listed investment, not from operations. Its growth narrative has relied on a sequence of approval-dependent JVs that have each slipped by one to three quarters. Its reported EPS of Rs 271.59 is computed on profit including minority interests [F] (AR2026 p.477), while our statements data shows Rs 236.61 [F] (NUMBERS). Even our bull DCF case, which assumes 43.5% starting growth and a 5.9% EBITDA margin never achieved historically, values the shares at about half the current price [F] (NUMBERS). The variant risk on the upside is a combination we cannot model from the disclosures: Vivo closing, PLI 2 at the 5% export band, and display margins in the mid-teens all arriving together in FY28 [AI].

blocks.text: [AI] Dixon is a 33-year-old company, but the business that drives today's valuation is very recent. Mobile and Other EMS was Rs 10,919 cr in FY24 and Rs 44,257 cr in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.106). Q Tech, Ismartu, Inventec, Longcheer, Signify and all three ECMS approvals date from August 2024 or later [F] (AR2026 p.141-146, p.514). The display plant, the Vivo JV, the Inventec plant and the Gemtek JV produced no revenue by Q1 FY27 [F] (CALL Aug 2026; ANNOUNCEMENTS). The track record that matters for the thesis is therefore under two years old. The legacy consumer-electronics and lighting businesses that built the 30-year record are now 6% of revenue or deconsolidated [F] (AR2026 p.78, p.505).

sections.title: Business model: where Dixon sits in the chain

items: 1. Brand customer awards a model or programme and specifies the bill of materials. In EMS mode the brand often controls key component sourcing such as memory [MC] (CALL May 2026).
2. Components are imported. Standalone CIF imports were Rs 2,064 cr [F] (AR2026 p.178-179). Group foreign-currency payables were Rs 8,198 cr, largely in USD, CNY and JPY [F] (AR2026 p.481-486).
3. Surface-mount PCB assembly, final assembly, testing and packing at Noida, Chennai, Tirupati and other plants [F] (AR2026 p.87).
4. In-house value-add steps: sheet metal and plastic moulding (since 2010), camera modules (Q Tech), and displays and SSDs (under construction) [MC] (AR2026 p.84; CALL Aug 2026).
5. Dispatch to brand (domestic) or export. Revenue recognised at a point in time [F] (AR2026 p.467).
6. PLI or other incentives accrue to Dixon as applicant. Part of them is passed to the customer: 'amount refundable to customers' was Rs 964 cr at FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.463).

blocks.text: [AI] Value capture is thin and structural. FY26 materials consumption (cost of materials plus inventory change) was about Rs 45,277 cr, roughly 92.6% of revenue [E] (AR2026 p.419). In Q1 FY27 cost of materials rose to 94.2% of operating revenue [F] (PPT Aug 2026). Dixon earns its return through asset turns rather than price: fixed-asset turnover was 11.7x in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). Components such as display (targeted mid-teens margin) [MC] (CALL May 2026) are the only route to higher value capture disclosed, and they are not yet producing.

Contractor wages and job work were Rs 432 cr in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.469-470). The group had 4,394 on-roll and 26,351 off-roll workers [F] (AR2026 p.77), so labour is heavily contract-based [AI]. Capex/sales was 2.2% in FY26 and 3.2-3.9% in FY22-FY24 [F] (NUMBERS). Factories are increasingly leased: right-of-use assets rose from Rs 569 cr to Rs 831 cr [F] (AR2026 p.418). The model is asset-light on fixed capital. The components push (display, Q Tech) raises capital intensity [AI].

blocks.text: [AI] Smartphone, feature-phone, IT hardware and telecom CPE assembly is commodity-like conversion. Dixon's edge is scale, approvals and policy-linked capacity, not product IP. The ODM lines (washing machines, refrigerators, TVs) carry Dixon-owned designs and earn higher percentage margins: Home Appliances 8.4% vs mobile 2.6% in Q1 FY27 [F] (PPT Aug 2026). They are small, though: 3% and 6% of revenue [F] (AR2026 p.78). Microwave radios, optical transceivers and displays could be differentiated, but today they rely on partner IP (Aviat licence, Gemtek, HKC) [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS; AR2026 p.141).

blocks.text: Annual segment margins are not disclosed. The consolidated accounts report a single segment, 'Electronics Goods', with no segment results or assets [F] (AR2026 p.497). Quarterly segment margins appear only in investor presentations [F] (PPT Aug 2026). Management declined to split telecom, wearables and Q Tech within Mobile & EMS [MC] (CALL May 2026), though it gave ad-hoc figures on later calls.

items: **Mobile & EMS.** Management cites memory-led price pass-through and share gains [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). [AI] FY26 growth of +33.9% includes the first full year of Ismartu (Rs 7,356 cr turnover), consolidation of Q Tech from 26 Sep 2025, and telecom growth from about Rs 3,600 cr to Rs 5,000 cr [F] (AR2026 p.514) [MC] (CALL May 2026). Organic smartphone growth was modest: volumes of about 32-33m in FY26 against 40-42m guided [MC] (CALL Oct 2025; CALL May 2026).

**Consumer Electronics.** Management cites GST-cut deferral, energy-norm transition and memory costs [MC] (CALL Oct 2025; CALL Feb 2026; CALL Aug 2026). [AI] Three consecutive years of decline suggest share loss or a deliberate de-emphasis, not only transient factors.

**Home Appliances.** Management cites capacity additions and new products [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). [AI] Growth is real but slow, and Q1 FY27 margin fell 310 bps on polymer and FX costs [F] (PPT Aug 2026), which undercuts the claim of full pass-through in ODM [MC] (CALL May 2026).

**Order-driven vs organic** [AI]: All segments are programme- and order-driven by nature. Mobile volumes are set by brand allocation, with 2-3 months of visibility [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Telecom depends on Airtel's capex cycle (related-party customer). Appliances are closest to organic demand-driven.

sections.title: Exports, domestic mix and trade exposure

blocks.text: Source: [F] (AR2026 p.467). The country split is not disclosed. Management names the US (anchor customer, understood to be Motorola) and Africa (Transsion via Ismartu) as destinations [MC] (CALL May 2026). Management put FY26 exports at about Rs 5,375 cr [MC] (CALL May 2026) against Rs 5,421 cr in the accounts [F] (AR2026 p.467). The two figures are close but not reconciled. Q1 FY27 exports were about Rs 1,100 cr, about 0.6-0.7m smartphones [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). A multi-year CAGR cannot be computed because only two years are disclosed.

[AI] The FY26 export jump is customer mix, not a broad strategy. It comes from one anchor's US programme and Ismartu's Africa shipments. The same anchor 'has started manufacturing with another EMS company' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), which exposes the export line to allocation shifts. Management expects FY27 export run-rate to be similar to FY26 [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Q1 FY27 at about Rs 1,100 cr is a lower quarterly run-rate than FY26's average of about Rs 1,355 cr [E].

items: **Currency.** Net foreign-currency exposure was Rs 7,552 cr, of which only Rs 142 cr of payables was hedged. A 1% move changes PBT by Rs 75.5 cr [F] (AR2026 p.481-486), about 3.6% of FY26 PBT [E]. Management says EMS is 'an absolute pass-through. So there is no currency risk' [MC] (CALL May 2026). Yet FX hurt Q Tech margins and the Q1 FY27 appliance margin [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The pass-through claim is not fully supported [AI].

**Tariffs.** Management says mobile phones are tariff-exempt in all markets, so the EU FTA (Jan 2026) helps lighting and TVs rather than phones [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). No dated US tariff measures affecting Dixon are disclosed in the documents.

**Location concentration.** Mobile manufacturing is concentrated in Noida (Sectors 60, 63, 68, 90) with an IT campus in Chennai [F] (AR2026 p.87). The new 1m sq ft anchor-customer facility is also in Noida [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). A regional disruption in the NCR would hit most of revenue [AI].

Our DCF model is a five-year FCFF projection from TTM sales of Rs 51,585 cr. FCFF is EBITDA less tax on EBIT, less capex, less change in net working capital. Growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate, followed by a Gordon terminal value; equity equals EV less borrowings [F] (NUMBERS). Capex equals depreciation plus new sales divided by a fixed-asset turnover of 10x. Working-capital days are set at zero. WACC is 15.0% (risk-free 7%, ERP 7%, beta 1.15), terminal growth 5.5%, tax 25.2%, and 6.117 cr shares [F] (NUMBERS).

Starting growth is 30%: the median of 3-year (58.9%), 5-year (49.9%) and TTM (5.5%) sales growth, capped at 30%. Growth fades to 10% by year 5. EBITDA margin is 3.9% and D&A 0.8% of sales [F] (NUMBERS). [AI] The 30% start is above management's own FY27 ex-Vivo target of about Rs 56,000 cr [MC] (CALL May 2026). The base case therefore implicitly assumes Vivo or export upside arrives.

[AI] The DCF penalises Dixon for what it is: a 3.9% EBITDA-margin business that must reinvest most of its operating cash to grow. With 15% WACC and capex tied to sales, FCFF is negligible until growth slows. Assumptions that cut both ways: excluding cash and other income understates value slightly, while ignoring NCI overstates it. Neither moves the result by more than a few hundred rupees per share against a gap of more than Rs 10,000.

The reverse DCF solves for constant five-year sales growth at the base 3.9% margin, the same WACC and terminal growth, that equates the DCF to today's EV. The answer is **about 84% a year for five years**, against a base-case 5-year CAGR equivalent of 19.8% [F] (NUMBERS). History: 3-year sales CAGR 58.9%, 5-year 49.9%, 9-year 39.4%; TTM growth over FY26 5.5% [F] (NUMBERS). The bull case starts at 43.5% and fades to 13% [F] (NUMBERS).

[AI] The price requires growth above Dixon's best-ever multi-year record, sustained for five more years from a base roughly 20x larger than FY17, at today's margin. Alternatively it requires a margin structure the company has never shown. Management's most ambitious target, Rs 1 lakh cr in 3-4 years [MC] (CALL Oct 2025), implies roughly 20-27% CAGR from FY26 [E], far below 84%.

[AI] The market may not value Dixon on a margin-constant DCF at all. It may be paying for: (1) a platform that compounds through repeated policy cycles; (2) components that could change the margin structure, with display targeted at mid-teens [MC] (CALL May 2026); (3) negative working capital, which makes growth nearly self-funding; and (4) scarcity value as India's largest listed EMS name. If EBITDA margin reached 6-7% on Rs 1 lakh cr revenue, the gap would narrow sharply. But that combination sits outside even our bull case, and nothing disclosed today evidences it.
